question.text: A certain pressure '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math>' is applied to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> litre of water and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> litre of a liquid separately. Water gets compressed to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn><mo>%</mo></math> whereas the liquid gets compressed to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>03</mn><mo>%</mo></math>. The ratio of Bulk modulus of water to that of the liquid is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______.

solution.text:
Bulk modulus is given by B=-ΔPΔVV

Now, in case of water,  Bwater=-ΔPΔVV=-ΔP0.01100

In case of liquid, Bliquid=-ΔP0.03100

Thus, the ratio BwaterBliquid=-ΔP0.0001-ΔP0.0003=3

Hence, the value of x=1.
